newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast prods firm on talk of refinery snag.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast prods firm on talk of refinery snag.

text.p: U.S. West Coast spot product prices advanced Thursday, lifted by bullish crude and heating oil futures and speculation a major Los Angeles refinery lost some diesel-making capacity.
ARCO late Wednesday denied rumors of equipment problems at its 265,000 barrel-per-day refinery at Carson, Calif..
But spot traders said the refinery bought in today's market, with one broker noting he alone helped the refinery purchase 25,000 barrels of diesel.
ARCO also declined to comment on why its CARB diesel rack prices, normally some of the cheapest in Los Angeles, firmed, according to traders.
Offers for CARB diesel in L.A. rose two cents from late Wednesday to 76 cents a gallon, brokers said, with a parcel sold at 75.50 cents.
Players talked Los Angeles CARB-grade unleaded gasoline one cent higher at 77/78 cents a gallon.
Conventional L.A. grade also rose one cent to 73/74 cents a gallon, traders said.
